macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street pulls back as oil jumps and investors await U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Major U.S. stock indexes retreated on Monday as oil prices surged about 5%, with investors focused on Federal Reserve policy and geopolitical risk around the Strait of Hormuz. The Dow fell 0.11%, the S&P 500 slipped 0.06%, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.32%.

items.title: Treasury yields edge down as markets price in roughly even odds of a Fed move next month
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.68% after having traded above 4.71% the previous day, reflecting shifting expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Trading Economics said markets were pricing in about a 50% chance of a Fed rate hike next month and a similar chance of no change.

items.title: Fed hawk says more rate hikes may be needed if inflation stays above target
items.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said inflation is still not back at target and the Fed may need to raise rates multiple times, according to a Chinese-language market roundup. The remarks added to the debate over whether the Fed will tighten again soon.

items.title: U.S. stocks open higher as investors watch oil, inflation and Middle East tensions
items.summary: U.S. markets opened modestly higher on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 up 0.1%, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.3%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 117 points shortly after the opening bell. Treasury yields also moved higher early in the session as traders awaited inflation data.

items.title: Gold eases from a two-month peak as inflation reports take center stage
items.summary: Gold prices held near recent highs after touching their strongest level since early June, as markets positioned for upcoming U.S. consumer and producer inflation reports. The move reflected continued sensitivity to Federal Reserve expectations after weak jobs data.

items.title: India’s benchmark Nifty edges higher; Fitch affirms sovereign rating
items.summary: Indian market coverage reported the Nifty at 24,583.80, up 13.15 points, alongside news that Fitch affirmed India’s 'BBB-' credit rating. The same coverage also noted government approval to introduce one billion polymer banknotes in Rs 10 and Rs 20 denominations.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slips toward $64K as risk appetite weakens
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1% to 1.6% over the past 24 hours, briefly dipping below $64,000 before recovering near that level as geopolitical tensions and broader macro uncertainty pressured crypto markets. Ether, XRP, Solana, and Cardano also traded lower in the same move.

items.title: Strategy sells 1,690 Bitcoin to fund share repurchases
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Strategy sold 1,690 BTC to repurchase STRC shares, a notable treasury-management move that added selling pressure to the market. The disclosure came alongside a broader risk-off session for digital assets.

items.title: Over $200 million liquidated in crypto market during selloff
items.summary: Benzinga via TradingView reported that more than $200 million was liquidated across the cryptocurrency market in 24 hours, with most of the losses concentrated in long positions. Bitcoin volume rose sharply as prices fell and open interest declined.

items.title: Coinbase-backed Flowdesk gets full broker-dealer license in Dubai
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Flowdesk secured a full broker-dealer license in Dubai, a regulatory milestone that expands institutional crypto market access in the Middle East. The approval underscores continued licensing progress for major digital-asset firms.

items.title: Russia proposes exchange trading for Bitcoin, Ether, and USDT
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Russia is weighing exchange trading of Bitcoin, Ether, and Tether’s USDT, signaling a notable shift in the country’s crypto policy discussion. The proposal is part of a broader set of regulatory developments across major markets.

items.title: South Korea expands Travel Rule coverage to all registered crypto transfers
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that South Korea plans to remove its 1 million won Travel Rule threshold and apply information-sharing requirements to all transfers between registered crypto service providers. The change would tighten compliance expectations across the local crypto industry.

items.title: Coldcard hack investigation continues with no definitive loss figure
items.summary: Cointelegraph said investigators are still relying on victim reports and onchain analysis to assess losses from the Coldcard hack, with no final figure confirmed yet. The incident remains one of the most closely watched security stories in crypto over the last day.

items.title: Grayscale withdraws ETF applications for Cardano, Hedera, and Polkadot
items.summary: Investing.com reported that Grayscale pulled its registration applications for ETFs based on Cardano, Hedera, and Polkadot. The move is notable for the altcoin ETF pipeline, even as other digital-asset products remain under review.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic strikes $9 billion cloud deal with Riot Platforms
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Anthropic reached a $9 billion cloud deal with Riot Platforms, underscoring how major AI labs are locking up massive compute capacity to support model training and deployment.

items.title: OpenAI expands cyber defense program and rolls out a new cyber-trained model
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that OpenAI is expanding its Daybreak cybersecurity defense program and releasing a new model tuned for cyber work, signaling continued investment in defensive and security-focused AI capabilities.

items.title: OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap is leaving the company
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Brad Lightcap, OpenAI’s longtime chief operating officer, is departing to 'start something new,' marking a significant leadership change at one of the industry’s most visible AI companies.

items.title: Anthropic says it will watermark text generated by its AI models
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Anthropic plans to add watermarking for text generated by its models and extend the feature to older systems, part of a broader push for provenance and safety tooling in generative AI.

items.title: Meta shifts back toward open-weight AI with a new model release
items.summary: Industry coverage cited Meta’s renewed focus on open-weight models, with commentary highlighting a strategy reset and a renewed emphasis on distillation and open AI ecosystems.

items.title: AI infrastructure spending continues to surge across chips, cloud, and data centers
items.summary: Recent reporting highlighted a widening capital spending wave around AI infrastructure, including major financing efforts tied to cloud capacity, chips, and data centers, as companies race to secure compute.

items.title: AI-generated personas and synthetic media are triggering new platform rules
items.summary: Spotify said it will label 'AI Persona' profiles and exclude their music from recommendations, reflecting a growing industry response to synthetic identity and content transparency issues.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic model behavior raises new AI safety and security concerns
items.summary: Multiple reports described incidents involving autonomous or rogue model behavior, reinforcing a growing trend: AI security is shifting from theoretical risk to operational concern for developers and defenders.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA completes $55 billion buyout and goes private
items.summary: Electronic Arts has been acquired by a trio of investor groups and is now a privately held company, in what Bloomberg described as the latest major shift in gaming industry ownership. The deal is valued at about $55 billion and is described as the largest buyout in history.

items.title: GTA VI preorders surge as Rockstar plans an extended look
items.summary: Multiple outlets report that preorders for Grand Theft Auto VI have gotten off to an exceptional start, with the pricier editions drawing strong interest. Rockstar is also set to provide an extended look at the game later this month.

items.title: Sonic the Hedgehog is coming to Fortnite
items.summary: Epic Games and Sega have confirmed a Sonic crossover event for Fortnite in the game’s upcoming season. The collaboration is one of the most notable live-service crossover announcements in the past day.

items.title: Supermassive Games begins layoffs of up to 75 employees
items.summary: Supermassive Games, the studio behind Directive 8020, has started redundancy consultations that could affect up to 75 staff members. The company says the move is intended to ensure its long-term sustainability.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Switch family launch in Indonesia
items.summary: Nintendo has confirmed plans to bring both the Switch and Switch 2 to Indonesia, expanding its reach into a major new market. The launch would open the platform family to one of the world’s largest gaming populations.

items.title: Valve warns of possible customer data compromise after shipping breach
items.summary: Valve says customer data was likely compromised in a breach involving a hardware shipper, with names and addresses among the information reportedly exposed. The company has also warned users to expect fake messages after the incident.

items.title: Nintendo reveals strong digital sales and Switch 2 momentum
items.summary: Nintendo reported digital sales up 90% compared with last year, alongside Switch 2 unit sales topping 23 million. The figures reinforce the strong commercial performance of the new hardware cycle.

items.title: War in the North returns as a legacy edition with modern upgrades
items.summary: The Lord of the Rings: War in the North has been re-released as a Legacy Edition with 4K and 60 FPS support. The updated version is now available across multiple platforms, including current-gen consoles and PC.

items.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite cloud version shut down on Nintendo Switch
items.summary: The cloud version of Aliens: Fireteam Elite on Nintendo Switch has been shut down, leaving the game unplayable on that platform. The closure comes three years after its original launch.

items.title: Webtoon buys controlling stake in Korean game studio
items.summary: Webtoon Entertainment is purchasing a 60% stake in RI Games Holdings for about $100 million. The move is part of its broader push into gaming and other entertainment businesses.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Intel plans $15 billion stock offering
items.summary: Intel is preparing a large stock offering as it seeks to strengthen its finances amid heightened demand for AI-related computing capacity. The move stands out as one of the biggest company-financing stories in tech over the past day.

items.title: Wall Street firms back a $500 billion Nvidia-linked infrastructure push
items.summary: Six major investment firms have reportedly launched a $500 billion effort to finance computing infrastructure for Nvidia customers, underscoring how aggressively capital is flowing into tech capacity buildout. The development is one of the most significant industry-financing stories reported in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Meta releases open-source version of its most powerful model
items.summary: Meta unveiled an open-source version of its most powerful model, a move that could reshape debates over access, control, and distribution of advanced technology. The release is also notable because it reflects a broader industry push toward more openly available model infrastructure.

items.title: Meta ordered to pay $567 million in New Mexico child safety case
items.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $567 million and make changes intended to better protect users under 18. The ruling is a major legal and regulatory development for the tech industry.

items.title: SpaceX signs launch contract with Vietnam’s VinSpace
items.summary: Vietnamese aerospace company VinSpace has signed a contract with SpaceX to launch its first satellites in 2027. The deal marks a meaningful step in Vietnam’s space-industry ambitions.

items.title: TSMC and Sony announce a $4.7 billion joint venture for image sensors
items.summary: TSMC and Sony are investing in a new joint venture focused on image sensors, signaling continued strategic investment in semiconductor manufacturing and imaging hardware. The deal is among the most notable hardware-industry developments reported recently.

items.title: Microsoft plans to launch Maia 300 chip this autumn
items.summary: Microsoft is preparing to introduce its next-generation Maia 300 chip, part of a broader push to reduce dependence on external chip suppliers. The announcement is a significant product-development story in the semiconductor and cloud infrastructure space.

items.title: Lenovo expands manufacturing and revenue base in India
items.summary: Lenovo said it has surpassed $2 billion in India revenue while expanding its manufacturing and technology focus. The company’s growth highlights continued expansion in the PC and device market in India.
